title: He Is 15. His Mother Wakes at 3 AM for His Cricket. The BCCI Just Told His Parents They Can Come Along.
excerpt: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest player ever picked for India's senior squad. The BCCI will fly his parents with him to Ireland and England and cover all their expenses.
body:
His mother wakes up at 3 AM every day to manage his cricket routine, nutrition and schedule. His father sold farmland and travelled hundreds of kilometres multiple times a week to get him to practice. On Saturday, the BCCI told Sanjeev and Aarti Sooryavanshi they could come along for the ride.

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, became the youngest player ever selected for India's senior cricket squad when the BCCI named him in three separate teams — the T20I squads for the upcoming tours of Ireland and England, and the Asian Games 2026 roster. Hours later, the board announced a decision that mattered as much as the selection itself: his parents would travel with him, and the BCCI would cover all their expenses.

"As he is a child, we have decided to allow his parents to accompany him to Ireland and England, so that they can be with him and help him settle in the new environment," BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia told Sportstar. "The Board will cover all their expenses."

## The Prithvi Shaw Precedent

The BCCI's decision is not merely administrative. It reflects hard lessons learned from Indian cricket's past experiments with teenage prodigies.

Prithvi Shaw was hailed as the next Sachin Tendulkar at 10. He made his India debut at 18 and remains the second-youngest Indian to score a Test hundred, after Tendulkar himself. But the weight of expectation, combined with sudden fame and the absence of a protective buffer, contributed to a career that has stalled. Shaw has not played for India since 2021 or in the IPL since 2024.

The board does not want a repeat. Its leadership has studied how other sports handle teenage talent — Jennifer Capriati reached the tennis world's top 10 at 14, only to be arrested for drug possession at 18 after fame consumed her adolescence. The BCCI's institutional memory extends to its own success stories, too. In 1989, when a 16-year-old Sachin Tendulkar debuted in Pakistan, his elder brother Ajit accompanied him on the tour. That arrangement is widely credited with helping Tendulkar stay grounded during the most formative period of his career.

## The IPL Sensation From Bihar

Sooryavanshi's trajectory has been extraordinary. The left-handed opener from Samastipur, Bihar, dominated IPL 2026 for the Rajasthan Royals — finishing with the most runs, the most sixes, and the highest strike rate of any batter in the tournament. His 776 runs came at a strike rate of 237.30. He hit 72 sixes across the season, breaking a record that had belonged to Chris Gayle. Five individual awards followed: Orange Cap, MVP, Emerging Player, Super Striker, and Most Sixes.

The "A" hand sign that became his signature celebration during the IPL was a tribute to his mother, Aarti. It was his way of honouring the sacrifices she made — the 3 AM wake-ups, the meal planning around his training schedule, the quiet, relentless work that made his cricket possible.

His father, Sanjeev, has already planned to be with him in Sri Lanka, where Sooryavanshi is currently training with the India A squad ahead of a tri-nation 50-over series starting June 9 in Dambulla. But the BCCI's formal arrangement for the Ireland and England tours goes further — it embeds parental support into the official touring structure.

## What It Means for NRI Families

The decision resonates beyond cricket. For the Indian diaspora, the image of immigrant parents sacrificing everything for a child's dream is deeply familiar. The Sooryavanshis' story — a family from small-town Bihar whose son is now representing India — mirrors the experience of countless NRI families who have uprooted their lives for their children's futures.

The BCCI's willingness to financially support that family unit during a critical transition sends a signal about how Indian institutions are beginning to understand the emotional infrastructure that underpins elite performance. It is a small, practical decision. It may also be one of the most consequential the board has made this year.

## What Comes Next

Sooryavanshi will first play the India A tri-series in Sri Lanka from June 9 to 21, where he joins a squad captained by Tilak Varma. He is then expected to fly to Ireland for India's two-match T20I series in late June, followed by a five-match T20I series in England in July. The Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya follow in September.

At every stop, his parents will be there. The BCCI has ensured that the youngest cricketer to wear India's colours will not have to navigate the biggest transition of his life alone.
